description: Crossfades two signals and then attenuates or inverts the result, with a control input for each, following the polyphony of whichever input has more channels

params.text: Mixes between the two signal inputs: all of input A at the bottom of its travel and all of input B at the top
Scales the crossfade control input before it is added to the crossfade knob; 10V at full amount covers the whole sweep
Scales the mixed signal: silence at the centre and the signal untouched at the top, and below centre the signal is replaced by its distance from 10V, so 0V comes out as 10V
Scales the attenuverter control input before it is added to the attenuverter knob; 5V at full amount moves it by a whole unit, which is half its travel

inputs.text: Input A of the crossfade, the one heard on its own with the crossfade knob turned down
Input B of the crossfade, the one heard on its own with the crossfade knob turned up
Moves the crossfade, scaled by the crossfade CV knob, a tenth of the sweep per volt at full amount
Moves the attenuverter, scaled by the attenuverter CV knob, a fifth of a unit per volt at full amount

outputs.text: The crossfaded and scaled signal, with as many channels as the wider of the two inputs

notes: the attenuverter starts at the centre, which is silence, so nothing comes out of a fresh module until it is turned
the inversion below centre is not a sign flip: the output is the signal's distance from 10V, scaled, which turns a 0 to 10V envelope upside down but does something else to audio

inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
